items.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020
items.q: Miles had Coltrane and Hank Mobley. So I always was attracted to it from the trumpet records I had.

ctx.x: You know this has been a fascinating conversation. I haven’t asked you why you were compelled to take up the saxophone.

You know I always loved it because I was into Miles and Clifford Brown and they had — Clifford had Sonny Rollins and Miles had Coltrane and Hank Mobley. So I always was attracted to it from the trumpet records I had. So I was endorsing trumpets for LeBlanc. I was 13 years old, and I asked Vito Pascucci, I said, “Can you send me a tenor?” And he sent me a Noblet tenor and it was so — I mean it struck me now even, it was so heavy and big that’s why I switched to alto. But I loved the tenor and that’s how it…
No I’d love to hear it.
